subject: chemistry-9
description: Authentic 12-mark Section A Federal Board examination simulator covering Periodic Table, Chemical Bonding, Organic Chemistry, and Hydrocarbons.

questions.question: An acyclic hydrocarbon with molecular formula C₆H₁₂ must contain:
questions.explanation: The formula C₆H₁₂ conforms to CnH2n (alkenes), indicating the presence of one carbon-carbon double bond (or a cycloalkane ring).

questions.question: In IUPAC organic nomenclature, the prefix “Hex-” denotes a parent chain of how many carbon atoms:
questions.explanation: In organic chemistry root names: Meth- (1), Eth- (2), Prop- (3), But- (4), Pent- (5), Hex- (6), Hept- (7), Oct- (8).

questions.question: In which of the following functional groups is a divalent oxygen atom bonded directly to two alkyl groups (R–O–R′):
questions.explanation: Ethers have the general structure R–O–R′, where an oxygen atom bridges two hydrocarbon radical groups.

questions.question: Which of the following non-metals exists as a lustrous, purple-black solid that sublimes upon gentle heating:
questions.explanation: Iodine (I2) is a halogen non-metal with metallic luster that readily undergoes sublimation into violet vapor.

questions.question: Which element belongs to Group 17 (Halogens) of the periodic table?
questions.explanation: Group 17 elements (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine, astatine) are called halogens because they form salts with alkali metals.

questions.question: Moving from left to right across a period in the modern periodic table, the first ionization energy generally:

options.B: Increases due to higher effective nuclear charge

questions.explanation: Across a period, nuclear charge increases while valence electrons are added to the same shell, drawing electrons closer and increasing ionization energy.

questions.question: In the formation of the ionic compound aluminum fluoride (AlF₃), each aluminum atom:

options.B: Loses 3 electrons to achieve neon configuration

questions.explanation: Aluminum has electronic configuration 2, 8, 3. It donates 3 valence electrons to three fluorine atoms, forming Al³⁺ cation with stable noble gas configuration.

questions.question: Which element in the periodic table possesses the highest Pauling electronegativity value (4.0):
questions.explanation: Fluorine has the highest electronegativity (4.0) because of its small atomic radius and high effective nuclear attraction for shared electron pairs.

questions.question: Carbon has 4 valence electrons and is located in which group of the periodic table:
questions.explanation: Carbon (atomic number 6) has configuration 1s² 2s² 2p² and belongs to Group 14 (IVA).

questions.question: Which of the following compounds exhibits ionic bonding with a giant crystal lattice:
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride is formed by complete electron transfer from Na to Cl, creating strong electrostatic attraction in a 3D ionic lattice.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as an alkaline earth metal (Group 2):
questions.explanation: Group 2 elements (beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium, radium) are known as alkaline earth metals.

questions.question: A coordinate covalent (dative) bond is present in which of the following species:
questions.explanation: In NH₄⁺, the ammonia molecule shares its lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom with a proton (H⁺), forming a coordinate covalent bond.
